title: Telemetry gap root cause hunt and alert throttle - WIP
content:
Summary:

This doc captures our on-call notes, initial investigation, mitigation steps, and follow-ups from the Nov 4-5 2024 telemetry gap that produced a large volume of noisy SLO burn alerts and missing host metrics across hosted API fleets. Purpose is to record hypotheses tried, short-term workarounds we applied, and proposed permanent fixes. This is intentionally a working log; expect edits.

High-level impact:
- Period: ~2024-11-04 23:40 UTC to 2024-11-05 02:05 UTC (total ~2h25m)
- Symptoms: sudden disappearance of multiple host-level metrics (cpu_usage, prometheus_agent:exporter_queue_length, network_io) for many regions; synthetic heartbeat metric (telemetry.heartbeat) stopped for a subset of hosts; rapid SLO-burn alerts for model-inference-latency and request-error-rate firing in waves (no upstream traffic spike).
- User-visible: elevated 99p latency for some tenants and transient increase in 5xxs for routed fallback model variants. Several customers reported degraded performance via console support tickets.

Detection timeline (key events):
- 2024-11-04 23:38 UTC: Observability platform flagged >10% missing-series anomaly for host metrics (alert: missing-metric-cascade).
- 23:40 UTC: Oncall (Asha) sees multiple SLO-burn alerts for hosted-api/us-west and eu-west clusters; paging begins.
- 23:46 UTC: Slack thread #sre-incidents created; initial triage — look at exporter logs and remote_write metrics.
- 23:54 UTC: Found exporter (telemetry-agent v2.3.1) restart on a subset of nodes; exporter logs show repeated 429s from remote_write endpoint followed by local queue overflow.
- 00:06 UTC: Correlation discovered: a customer onboarding job started ~23:36 UTC that created a burst of high-cardinality traces/metrics from an internal tooling service (onboard-job).
- 00:20 UTC: Mitigation 1: temporarily muted low-signal SLOs (per mute playbook) and scaled up remote_write workers for the critical ingestion path.
- 01:02 UTC: Short-term fix: restart telemetry-agent on affected hosts with increased local queue size; synthetic heartbeat restored gradually.
- 02:05 UTC: All major host metrics returned; alerts subsided.

Investigation notes and evidence: 
- Prometheus remote_write reported sustained 429s starting 23:37 UTC; rate-limit hit on the downstream write sampler.
- telemetry-agent queue_length metric grew until OOM/flow-control kicked in; exporter entered a backpressure mode and stopped exporting many series (resulting in missing metrics).
- The onboarding job created ~80k new metric series (high-cardinality labels) within 2 minutes — exceeded ingest pipeline cardinality filters and caused the write throttle to reject batches.
- Alert storms were amplified by rule configuration that evaluated on missing-series deltas (we treat missing-series as immediate SLO burn trigger), combined with alerting rules that had short windows (1m) and no internal suppression.
- We confirmed no upstream model-serving degradation independently — the increased SLO burn was a function of missing telemetry used by SLO calculation (synthetic_inference_latency fallback to host_cpu proxy) which was biased.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
1) A high-cardinality burst from the onboarding job flooded the telemetry pipeline.
2) The remote_write endpoint started rate-limiting (429), exporter queues grew, and the telemetry-agent switched to a degraded export mode that dropped series rather than applying a safe tail-sampling policy.
3) Missing-series detectors and aggressive SLO calculation rules interpreted absence of host metrics as latency degradation, causing rapid SLO-burn alerts and noisy paging.
4) No automatic circuit breaker existed between onboarding job ingestion and the critical host-metrics tenant, so overload impacted core observability streams.

Immediate mitigations performed (commands / actions taken during incident):
- Quieted noisy alerts: used /mute to throttle missing-series and SLO-burn alerts for 30m windows (see slack thread).
- Restarted telemetry-agent on affected hosts with increased --queue-capacity=50000 and enabled experimental tail-sampler flag to preserve representative series.
- Scaled remote_write ingestion workers from 6 -> 10 in prod for 1 hour to absorb backpressure.
- Kicked off emergency job to identify and stop the offending onboarding job (identified by trace ids and cluster tags) — onboarding job paused by platform team.
- Rolled out a temporary alert dedupe rule that batches missing-series alerts by region for 10 minutes to reduce paging.

Runbook gaps identified (things to fix in runbook text):
- No documented quick-check command to identify high-cardinality bursts by job name; current runbook assumes only node-level failures. Need a step: `kubectl logs --selector=job=onboard-job -n platform-tools` and `promql: topk(50, increase(metric_series_total[2m]))` as a first-responder.
- Missing guidance on whether to increase exporter queue vs restart; decision tree should include fallback to tail-sampling.
- Lack of an explicit circuit-breaker step to temporarily quarantine noisy tenants or jobs.

Short-term action items (owners + due dates):
- SRE: Add a 10-minute alert throttling automaton for missing-series and SLO-burn alerts (JIRA:SRE-4821) — Owner: Diego Morales — Due: 2024-11-12.
- Platform: Add onboard-job rate limiter in job-runner service; ensure per-tenant ingestion caps (JIRA:PLAT-998) — Owner: Lina Zhou — Due: 2024-11-19.
- Telemetry: Enable tail-sampling by default in telemetry-agent and increase graceful queue sizing (PR #312) — Owner: Ravi Menon — Due: 2024-11-15.
- Observability: Add synthetic heartbeat watcher with auto-repair playbook step (see linked confluence page) — Owner: Megan O'Neill — Due: 2024-11-20.

Long-term proposals (discussion items):
- Ingress-side circuit breaker: implement per-tenant cardinality caps and soft-deny with 429 cascading to job-runner; separate critical host metrics tenant to a protected path.
- Alerting rework: change missing-series SLO calculations to incorporate a grace window (default 5m) and use aggregated rollups instead of raw series for SLO burn triggers. Add adaptive suppression: if >x% series missing but synthetic_heartbeat present, suppress SLO immediate paging.
- Telemetry-agent improvements: graceful degradation mode should tail-sample instead of dropping series; add backpressure signals to job-runner to slow high-cardinality producers.
- Runbook automation: add a runbook-play executor that can apply temporary mute/dedupe and automatically annotate incidents with the exact command used.

Proposed updated runbook excerpt (draft):
[Quick checklist for missing-series / metric blackhole]
1) Check synthetic heartbeat: `sum(last_over_time(telemetry_heartbeat[5m]))` — if heartbeat absent, treat as host-level outage and follow host-recovery steps.
2) Identify high-cardinality producer: `topk(20, increase(metric_series_total[2m]))` and map to pod/job labels.
3) If onboarding-job or similar found, pause job and create artifact in PLAT ticketing system; escalate to platform team.
4) If remote_write 429s present, increase worker pool (if autoscaling disabled) and enable tail-sample on telemetry-agent; consider controlled restart.
5) Mute missing-series alerts for 10m while mitigation occurs; do not mute SLO burn alerts for critical customer tenants without approval.

Postmortem artifacts to produce (owners):
- Full postmortem doc for public internal review (confluence) — Owner: Asha Patel — Due: 2024-11-25.
- Telemetry-agent PRs for queue/backpressure changes — Owner: Ravi Menon — Due: 2024-11-15.
- Alerting rule revamp RFC (include graceful windows and dedupe logic) — Owner: Diego Morales — Due: 2024-12-01.

Notes / open questions:
- Should missing-series be considered a first-class SLO input? We currently treat it as such and it produced false-positive SLO burns during telemetry pipeline failures. Proposal: compute SLOs using both raw-series and synthetic probe fallback; prefer probe when raw-series health is below threshold.
- How do we balance quick muting to reduce pager fatigue vs visibility for real degradations? Need an automated, auditable mute that records reason and TTL.

Appendix - useful queries & commands used during triage:
- promql: `increase(prometheus_remote_write_429_total[5m])`
- promql: `topk(50, increase(metric_series_total[2m])) by(job)`
- k8s: `kubectl -n telemetry get pods -l app=telemetry-agent -o wide`
- logs: `kubectl logs <telemetry-agent-pod> -n telemetry | grep -i "429" -C 5`

Slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C0ABCDEFQ/p1699161600000000
Confluence draft: confluence:Telemetry-Gap-Incident-2024
Jira tickets: SRE-4821, PLAT-998, OBS-317
GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-agent/pull/312

Status: working draft. Next step is to convert this into the full incident postmortem and schedule a 90-minute blameless review with platform, telemetry, and SRE teams to lock down owners and dates.
